design_scope.purpose: Freeze a defensible multi-panel development design before any new MEPS outcome access.

source_basis.evidence_boundary: The records above freeze candidate panel identity, panel number, and calendar-year metadata only. They do not establish cross-panel variable equivalence, collection-mode comparability, or a common LONGWT target population. Those claims require the per-panel Gate 15 source and schema review.

conditions: Official AHRQ metadata identifies the file as the specified two-year longitudinal PUF and confirms its panel number and consecutive calendar years.
The panel has the same person-level two-year longitudinal unit and five-round participation concept as the canonical cohort contract.

Official documentation supports semantic equivalence for the eligibility fields, baseline coverage months, follow-up coverage months, 74 baseline predictors, protected audit variables, LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU.
The panel-specific LONGWT target population can be stated from its official documentation and is compatible with the frozen panel-specific estimand.

Collection mode, response, instrument, and calendar-year differences do not invalidate the prespecified descriptive comparison; unresolved differences fail the design rather than trigger post-outcome panel selection.
Panel and household/person identifiers can be namespaced without any record linkage or re-identification attempt.

panel_selection.failure_action: fail_closed_and_escalate; do not silently drop a candidate because its observed event count is inconvenient
panel_selection.three_or_four_year_files: excluded; the common design is exactly a consecutive two-calendar-year estimand

canonical_estimand.unit: one person in one panel-specific two-year longitudinal PUF
canonical_estimand.panel_specific_target: The civilian noninstitutionalized population represented by that panel's official two-year longitudinal target population after the frozen eligibility restrictions; not an unrestricted all-adults population claim.
canonical_estimand.baseline_period: the first calendar year of each candidate panel
canonical_estimand.follow_up_period: the immediately following calendar year of the same candidate panel
eligibility: 18 <= AGEY1X <= 64 at the end of baseline Year 1
all 12 baseline INS<month>Y1X values equal the documented insured code 1

primary_outcome.name: any_uninsured_month_y2
primary_outcome.construction: at least one of the 12 follow-up INS<month>Y2X values equals the documented uninsured code 2
primary_outcome.negative_definition: all 12 follow-up monthly values equal the documented insured code 1

sensitivity_outcomes: at least three follow-up months with the documented uninsured code
follow-up December uninsured using the documented month-12 field

gate_15_must_verify: valid, missing, negative, and unknown codes
numeric versus categorical type and scale
collection mode and response changes, especially Panel 25
semantic_alignment_contract.mapping_failure_action: fail_closed; no renaming or recoding based only on matching column names

longwt_and_pooling.within_panel_longwt_meaning: Use the official panel-specific LONGWT only after Gate 15 confirms that it represents the documented two-year longitudinal target population for that PUF and the frozen eligibility domain.
longwt_is_not: a common weight scale across panels by default

primary_population_estimation.reporting: Report each panel's weighted estimate and design-adjusted uncertainty separately. Do not publish a pooled population estimate from concatenated records.

raw_concatenation.reason: Different panel-specific longitudinal target populations and repeated calendar years are not made into one population by row binding.

simple_division_by_panel_count.reason: Dividing LONGWT by the number of panels has no frozen population interpretation.

development_model_loss_only.per_panel_weight: v_pi = LONGWT_pi / sum(LONGWT_pj over the eligible records in the same panel and same loss partition)
development_model_loss_only.aggregate_objective: L = (1/K) * sum over panels p of [sum_i(v_pi * loss_i) / sum_i(v_pi)]
development_model_loss_only.implementation_requirement: Compute each panel loss separately and then take the prespecified panel-balanced mean. Never replace this with raw LONGWT over concatenated rows or LONGWT divided by K.
development_model_loss_only.population_claim: The resulting loss is a development/model-selection criterion, not a claim about a pooled US population total.

longwt_and_pooling.future_pooled_population_estimate: not defined in Gate 14A; requires a new explicit estimand and official target-mass justification

partitioning.fit_boundary: fit preprocessing and initial models on train only; select on validation; refit only after choices are frozen; use calibration only for calibration

alternatives_considered.description: Fit a separate model in each panel and report panel-specific estimates.
Fit one common model across the accepted development panels using the explicit within-panel normalized LONGWT panel-balanced loss; PANEL is a namespace and validation stratum, not a predictor.
Re-evaluate the selected common model separately within each panel using the original panel-specific LONGWT, plus the prespecified unweighted and outcome-definition sensitivities.
For each panel, train the common development model without that panel and evaluate only on the held-out development panel, with no tuning on the held-out panel.

development_validation.selection_rationale: It increases development diversity while preserving panel-specific estimands at evaluation: panel-aware normalization prevents one panel's weight scale from dominating model fitting, and all primary estimates remain separately weighted by the original panel LONGWT.
development_validation.selection_rule: No data-driven panel selection: freeze model, preprocessing, mitigation arm, and threshold decisions using only the prespecified panel-balanced validation criterion and panel-specific diagnostics. Never select or remove a panel after viewing its event count.
development_validation.calibration_boundary: Calibration is fit only after model choices are frozen, on the calibration partition within the selected design. Same-partition calibration diagnostics are apparent calibration-fit evidence, not out-of-sample validation. Any change to the existing threshold transfer rule requires a later explicit decision.
development_validation.reporting_boundary: Always retain panel-specific utility, calibration, fairness, and uncertainty outputs. A macro-average may summarize panel-specific quantities only when labeled as a panel-balanced descriptive summary, never as a pooled population estimate.

required_power_report: total eligible positive events across the fixed development set
eligible positive and negative events for each panel
unweighted subgroup n, positive events, negative events, and Kish effective n for every primary audit cell
secondary-cell suppression status using the frozen rules

estimability_rules.secondary_suppression: mark unavailable; no post-outcome ad hoc merging

power_and_estimability.underpowered_action: stop before model development and keep Panel 27 locked

repeated_calendar_years.policy: Treat overlapping calendar years as correlated historical context, not duplicate independent observations. Keep panel labels and panel-specific estimates; do not deduplicate or link people across panels.

review_topics: pandemic-era collection mode and instrument changes
comparability of eligibility, predictor, outcome, and survey-design semantics
panel_25.unresolved_difference_action: fail_closed; no post-outcome exclusion or reweighting

locked_holdout.unlock_condition: Only a later independent Gate 17 audit may decide whether to unlock; Gate 18 may evaluate once after an explicit Gate 17 ACCEPT.

gate_15_entry_and_stop_rules.entry: Only after Codex accepts this metadata-only design; Gate 15 proceeds one panel at a time.
allowed_first_checks: official source URL, file size, SHA-256, and download manifest
documented variable semantics and coding maps
weight, strata, PSU, identifier, and calendar-year structure
gate_15_entry_and_stop_rules.outcome_access_sequence: Only after structural closure and explicit Codex acceptance may the authorized worker compute safe aggregate queue and event counts for a development panel.
stop_if: core variables cannot be semantically unified
LONGWT target population cannot be defended per panel
Panel 25 pandemic-era differences invalidate the prespecified comparison
the fixed development design has fewer than 200 positive events
a required primary subgroup is not estimable
any cross-panel identifier, design-variable, weight, or leakage check fails

required_synthetic_cases: multiple panels with colliding raw DUID, PID, or PSU values
Panel 27 lock remains true even when synthetic total events reach 200
